description: Rules from spec/90-extensions/spdx.md: the opt-in bridge that cites the bill of materials describing an artifact's contents (SPDX-1..SPDX-6). Every vector names the bridge it exercises (CON-28), so an implementation that does not claim it skips them. SPDX-7 and SPDX-8 are consumer obligations and are exempted in exemptions.json. The base claim points at fixtures/hello.spdx.json, a real SPDX 2.3.1 document whose checksums tests/test_validate.py recomputes from fixtures/hello.txt.

vectors.name: spdx/claim-must-be-an-object
vectors.description: A bare namespace leaves no room for the edition or the element, and cannot be distinguished from a string another extension might define.

vectors.name: spdx/claim-must-not-be-null
vectors.description: JSON null is not an object and not an absent member: a record that writes the key with no claim is rejected, exactly as the schema types it.

vectors.name: spdx/version-is-required
vectors.description: SPDX 3.0 replaced the document model, so a claim that names no edition cannot say which one its fields mean.

vectors.name: spdx/version-must-be-a-covered-edition
vectors.description: 3.0 is a different document model — spdxId as an IRI, namespaceMap, checksums behind verifiedUsing — and citing it under 2.3 rules would be a claim nobody specified.

vectors.name: spdx/document-is-required
vectors.description: A claim that names no document points at nothing; the namespace is the only thing that makes the SBOM findable.

vectors.name: spdx/document-must-carry-a-scheme
vectors.description: Section 6.5 requires a scheme: the namespace is an absolute URI, and a bare path is not one.

vectors.name: spdx/document-must-not-carry-a-fragment
vectors.description: SPDX reserves '#' to build element URIs, so a namespace that already carries one cannot be read unambiguously (sections 6.5, 7.2).

vectors.name: spdx/element-must-be-a-local-spdxid
vectors.description: An element of another document is written DocumentRef-x:SPDXRef-y (section 6.6), but the claim names one document and has no member for a second one.

vectors.name: spdx/element-must-not-carry-a-plus
vectors.description: DocumentRef idstrings allow '+', element SPDXIDs do not (sections 6.6, 7.2); the bridge follows the element rule.

vectors.name: spdx/element-must-not-carry-an-underscore
vectors.description: The prose (sections 7.2, 8.2) and the published SPDX 2.3.1 JSON schema agree on letters, digits, '.' and '-', so an underscore is not an SPDX element identifier in either rendering.

vectors.name: spdx/element-must-not-be-the-document-identifier
vectors.description: SPDXRef-DOCUMENT is well formed and a category error as a subject: a document is not one of the things it describes, and the claim without 'element' already says 'the document, no particular element'.

vectors.name: spdx/claim-defines-three-members
vectors.description: The tempting fourth member is a copy of an SPDX checksum, which can be numerically right while the record goes stale; a checksum belongs to the document that owns it.

vectors.name: spdx/id-must-not-be-the-document-namespace
vectors.description: A namespace is a name that changes when the document is reissued and that no reader can derive from the artifact's bytes (SPDX-6); 'id' stays urn:variorum:sha256:... (ID-7).

vectors.name: spdx/id-must-not-be-an-element-uri
vectors.description: SPDX builds an element URI from the namespace, '#', and the SPDXID (section 7.2). It identifies an element inside one document version, not the bytes in hand.

vectors.name: spdx/document-only-claim-is-accepted
vectors.description: Without 'element' the claim says the artifact is in the document's scope and names no element; that is the weaker claim, and it is legitimate.

vectors.name: spdx/element-naming-a-package-is-accepted
vectors.description: The bridge does not assume the element is a file: a package element is a legitimate subject, and what a reader may compare then differs (SPDX-7).

vectors.name: spdx/element-idstring-accepts-dots-and-uppercase
vectors.description: The idstring is letters, digits, '.' and '-' with no case constraint (section 7.2); a validator that insisted on lowercase would reject identifiers SPDX allows.

vectors.name: spdx/a-record-without-the-claim-says-nothing
vectors.description: An unclaimed record for an artifact that happens to be listed in an SBOM is still a core record; the bridge is opt-in, and silence is not a denial.
